items.title: Ketamine for Co-occurring Chronic Pain and Depression: A Scoping Review fing the Dual-Outcome Evidence Gap and Its Treatment and Research Implications.

summaries.en: When chronic pain and depression show up together—which happens surprisingly often—they're actually tangled up in the brain in ways we're just beginning to understand. A new review found that ketamine, a drug already known to lift depression, might also ease chronic pain at the same time. This matters because treating both conditions with one medicine could be genuinely transformative for people stuck in that painful, heavy place. Researchers looked at 12 studies from the past two decades where patients got ketamine and had both their pain and mood measured afterward. Most showed improvement in both, though the studies varied wildly in how they worked and who they treated. This gap—the fact that we don't yet have clear, standardized evidence—actually points to something exciting: psychedelics research is moving beyond single-symptom solutions toward understanding how these medicines might rewire multiple problems at once. That's the frontier we're heading into.
summaries.da: Når kronisk smerte og depression dukker op sammen—hvilket sker oftere end man tror—er de faktisk sammenvævet i hjernen på måder, vi først nu begynder at forstå. En ny gennemgang fandt, at ketamin, et stof der allerede vides at løfte depression, måske også kan lindre kronisk smerte samtidigt. Det betyder noget, fordi at behandle begge tilstande med én medicin kunne være rigtig transformativt for mennesker fanget i det smertefulde, tunge sted. Forskere kiggede på 12 studier fra de seneste to årtier, hvor patienter fik ketamin og fik målt både deres smerte og sindstilstand bagefter. De fleste viste forbedring i begge dele, selvom studierne varierede vildt i deres tilgang og hvem de behandlede. Det hul—det faktum at vi endnu ikke har klare, standardiserede beviser—peger faktisk på noget spændende: psykedelika-forskningen bevæger sig ud over enkelt-symptom-løsninger mod at forstå, hvordan disse stoffer kan omstrukturere flere problemer på én gang. Det er grænselandet, vi bevæger os ind i.

items.title: Current perspectives in the pharmacological treatment of gambling disorder: psychedelics and beyond.

summaries.en: Gambling disorder traps people in a cycle that existing medications can't reliably break—but researchers are getting closer. A new review reveals that psychedelics like psilocybin and MDMA, along with ketamine, show real promise for rewiring the brain patterns that drive compulsive gambling, particularly the rigid thinking and dysregulated reward system that keeps people hooked. Scientists analyzed over a decade of pharmacological research to map out what actually works: while older drug approaches have limitations, these neuroplasticity-focused treatments target the root mechanisms differently—essentially helping the brain "unstick" from its addictive pathways. This research signals an important shift in how we think about behavioral addictions, moving beyond band-aid symptom relief toward genuine brain-level healing. As psychedelic science matures, we're watching addiction treatment evolve in real time.
summaries.da: Spilleafhængighed fanger mennesker i en cykel, som eksisterende medicin ikke pålideligt kan bryde—men forskere kommer tættere på løsningen. En ny oversigt viser, at psykedelika som psilocybin og MDMA, sammen med ketamin, viser reelt løfte for at omplante hjernens mønstre, der driver tvangsmæssigt gambling, især den stive tænkning og dysreguleret belønningssystem, der holder folk faste. Forskere analyserede over et årti af farmakologisk forskning for at kortlægge, hvad der virker: mens gamle medikamentelle tilgange har begrænsninger, retter disse neuroplasticitet-fokuserede behandlinger sig mod grundmekanismerne anderledes—og hjælper hjernens væsen med at "slippe fri" fra sine afhængighedsmønstre. Denne forskning signalerer et vigtigt skift i, hvordan vi tænker på adfærdsmæssige afhængigheder, væk fra plejestrips symptomletlindring mod ægte helbredelse på hjernens niveau. Når psykedelisk videnskab modnes, ser vi afhængighedsbehandling udvikle sig i realtid.

items.title: Adapted Massed Exposure Therapy Enhanced with MDMA for PTSD (aMETEMP): A randomized, double-masked protocol adapted for Veterans Affairs healthcare system.

summaries.en: Many veterans with PTSD don't get better with standard therapy alone — but a new study suggests adding MDMA to exposure therapy could change that. Researchers are testing whether MDMA helps people process trauma more deeply by making them less afraid and more emotionally open during treatment. This is a carefully designed pilot study with 20 veterans receiving a single MDMA session integrated into a focused 3-week therapy program, mostly delivered online to make it more accessible. It's a crucial next step: unlike earlier psychedelic PTSD research, this trial uses a proper control group and keeps participants genuinely blind to which treatment they're getting, making the results much more reliable and trustworthy for real-world use.
summaries.da: Mange veteraner med PTSD bliver ikke bedre af almindelig terapi alene — men et nyt studie tyder på, at psykedelika som MDMA kunne ændre det. Forskere tester, om MDMA hjælper mennesker med at bearbejde traumer dybere ved at gøre dem mindre bange og mere følelsesmæssigt åbne under behandling. Dette er et grundigt planlagt pilotprojekt med 20 veteraner, der får en enkelt MDMA-session integreret i et fokuseret 3-ugers terapiprogram, mest afviklet online for at gøre det mere tilgængeligt. Det er et afgørende næste skridt: i modsætning til tidligere psykedelika-PTSD-forskning bruger dette studie en rigtig kontrolgruppe og holder deltagerne virkelig uvidende om, hvilken behandling de får, hvilket gør resultaterne meget mere pålidelige for real-world brug.

items.title: Breaking: Compass Files Psilocybin for TRD New Drug Application with FDA

summaries.en:
Compass Pathways just filed psilocybin with the FDA as a potential treatment for treatment-resistant depression—a major milestone that could bring this psychedelic closer to becoming an actual medicine. For people whose depression hasn't budged despite trying multiple antidepressants, this represents real hope based on solid clinical research showing psilocybin can help where conventional drugs have failed.

The company submitted this New Drug Application after years of clinical trials testing psilocybin therapy in carefully controlled settings. This move signals that psychedelics are moving from the lab into the medical mainstream—we're watching the regulatory system begin to recognize what research has been showing: these substances, combined with proper therapy, might unlock treatment options for some of the hardest mental health challenges we face.
summaries.da:
Compass Pathways har netop indgivet ansøgning til FDA om at få psykedelika godkendt som behandling for behandlingsresistent depression—et kæmpe skridt, der kunne bringe denne substans tættere på at blive rigtig medicin. For mennesker hvis depression ikke har reageret på flere forskellige antidepressiva, betyder dette konkret håb baseret på solid forskning, der viser at psykedelika kan hjælpe hvor konventionelle lægemidler har slået fejl.

Selskabet indgav denne ansøgning efter år med kliniske forsøg, der testede psykedelika-terapi under kontrolerede betingelser. Dette signal betyder, at psykedelika bevæger sig fra laboratoriet ind i medicinen som sådan—vi ser det regulatoriske system begynde at anerkende det, som forskningen længe har vist: disse stoffer kan, kombineret med ordentlig terapi, åbne behandlingsmuligheder for nogle af vores hårdeste psykiske sundhedsudfordringer.

items.title: Working memory neural correlates after ketamine in treatment-resistant depression: a randomized placebo-controlled functional magnetic resonance imaging study.

summaries.en: Ketamine works fast against severe depression—but here's the surprise: it lifts mood without scrambling how your brain handles working memory. Researchers gave people with treatment-resistant depression either ketamine or a placebo, then scanned their brains while they did memory tasks. Depression scores dropped dramatically after ketamine, yet people performed just as well on the tasks as before. What changed was subtler: specific brain regions showed different activity patterns after ketamine, particularly in areas linked to attention and perception. This randomized, controlled study adds a crucial piece to the puzzle: ketamine's antidepressant magic doesn't come from fixing memory problems or broad cognitive damage—it's rewiring something more targeted in how the brain processes information during mood regulation.
summaries.da: Psykedelika virker hurtigt mod svær depression—men her kommer overraskelsen: det løfter humøret uden at ødelægge, hvordan din hjerne håndterer arbejdshukommelse. Forskere gav mennesker med behandlingsresistent depression enten psykedelika eller placebo og skanende deres hjerner mens de udfyldte hukommelsesopgaver. Depressionsscore faldt dramatisk efter psykedelika, men mennesker klarede opgaverne lige så godt som før. Det, der ændrede sig, var mere subtilt: specifikke hjernebområder viste forskellige aktivitetsmønstre efter psykedelika, især områder forbundet med opmærksomhed og perception. Dette randomiserede, kontrolleret studie tilføjer et afgørende puslespil: psykedelikas antidepressive magi kommer ikke fra at reparere hukommelsesproblem eller bred kognitiv skade—det ændrer noget mere målrettet i, hvordan hjernen regulerer humør.

items.title: MDMA-assisted therapy for social anxiety disorder: A randomized, open-label, wait-list controlled trial.

summaries.en: What if the thing that makes you feel connected at a concert could help heal social anxiety? A new study shows people with social anxiety who received MDMA-assisted therapy experienced dramatic improvements — their anxiety scores dropped by nearly 43 points on a standard measure, with effects far beyond what typically happens with waitlist controls. No serious side effects occurred. Researchers gave 20 participants three preparation sessions, two doses of MDMA with a therapist, and follow-up integration sessions over several months. This builds on earlier promising results and represents a crucial step: psychedelics aren't magic bullets, but when combined with skilled therapy in the right setting, they seem to help people access parts of themselves that were previously locked away by fear. We're watching the field move from "does this work?" to "how do we do this safely and effectively?" — and that's genuinely exciting.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis det, der får dig til at føle dig forbundet på en koncert, kunne hele social angst? Et nyt studie viser, at mennesker med social angst, der fik MDMA-assisteret terapi, oplevede dramatiske forbedringer — deres angstscorer faldt med næsten 43 point på en standardmåling, med effekter langt ud over hvad der typisk sker med ventelister. Ingen alvorlige bivirkninger opstod. Forskerne gav 20 deltagere tre forberedelsessessioner, to doser MDMA med en terapeut og opfølgende integrationsøkter over flere måneder. Dette bygger på tidligere lovende resultater og repræsenterer et afgørende skridt: psykedelika er ikke tryllekunst, men når de kombineres med dygtig terapi i det rigtige miljø, hjælper de mennesker med at få adgang til dele af sig selv, der tidligere var låst af frygt. Vi ser fagfeltet bevæge sig fra "virker det?" til "hvordan gør vi det sikkert og effektivt?" — og det er virkelig spændende.

items.title: Psychedelic modulation of excitation–inhibition balance and the Affective Core Self: A multilevel mechanistic framework

summaries.en:
What if the key to psychedelics' lasting effects on mood and self-perception lies in how they rebalance the brain's basic wiring? New research proposes that psychedelics work by fine-tuning the equilibrium between excitation and inhibition across multiple levels of the brain—from your nervous system's automatic responses to your deepest sense of self. This isn't just abstract neuroscience; it means psychedelics may literally reshape how your brain regulates emotions and processes who you are, potentially explaining why people report such profound shifts in wellbeing long after the experience ends.

Scientists integrated evidence from neuroimaging and pharmacology studies to build this mechanistic framework, mapping how a single molecular action (5-HT2A receptor activation) cascades through interconnected brain circuits. The finding fits squarely into where psychedelic research is heading: moving beyond describing what happens in the brain during a trip, toward actually understanding *why* these substances create lasting changes in how people feel and think about themselves. That's the kind of clarity that could transform how we use psychedelics therapeutically.
summaries.da:
Hvad hvis nøglen til psykedelikas langvarige effekter på humør og selvopfattelse ligger i, hvordan de genopretter hiernens grundlæggende balance? Ny forskning foreslår, at psykedelika virker ved at fintjustere ligevægten mellem aktivering og hæmning på flere niveauer i hjernen—fra dine autonome reaktioner til din dybeste selvfølelse. Dette er ikke blot abstrakt neurovidenskab; det betyder, at psykedelika kan bogstaveligt talt omforme, hvordan din hjerne regulerer følelser og opfatter, hvem du er—hvilket potentielt forklarer, hvorfor mennesker oplever så dybe forandringer i trivsel længe efter oplevelsen er forbi.

Videnskabsmænd integrerede fund fra hjernebilledning og farmakologistudier for at udvikle denne mekanistiske model, som kortlægger, hvordan en enkelt molekylær handling (5-HT2A receptoraktivering) bølger gennem sammenkoblede hjernekredse. Resultatet passer perfekt ind i, hvor psykedelikaforskningen er på vej: væk fra blot at beskrive hvad der sker i hjernen under en tur, hen imod faktisk at forstå *hvorfor* disse stoffer skaber vedvarende ændringer i, hvordan mennesker har det og tænker om sig selv. Dét er den klarhed, som kan transformere, hvordan vi bruger psykedelika terapeutisk.

items.title: Researchers' Experiences with IRB Oversight of Psychedelic Research.

summaries.en: Safety boards reviewing psychedelic research sometimes don't fully grasp what these substances actually do—but that's changing. Researchers who've navigated IRB approvals report that while review boards initially raised valid questions about participant safety and consent, many had misconceptions about psychedelics' risks. The good news? When researchers took time to educate their IRBs and build relationships, approvals moved forward smoothly. This matters because as psychedelic science accelerates toward real treatments for depression and PTSD, we need review systems that understand the science rather than fear the stigma. The study interviewed 20 US researchers about their IRB experiences, showing that knowledge-sharing between science and oversight bodies isn't just helpful—it's essential for getting promising research into the world.
summaries.da: Etikkomitéer, der godkender psykedelika-forskning, forstår ikke altid helt, hvad disse stoffer gør—men det er ved at ændre sig. Forskere, der har navigeret gennem godkendelsesprocesser, fortæller, at selvom komitéerne stillede vigtige spørgsmål om sikkerhed og samtykke, havde mange fejlagtige opfattelser af psykedelikas risici. Det gode nyt? Når forskere brugte tid på at uddanne deres komitéer og opbygge relationer, gik godkendelser gnidningsløst. Det er vigtigt, fordi når psykedelika-videnskaben accelererer mod rigtige behandlinger for depression og PTSD, skal vi have kontrolsystemer, der forstår videnskaben i stedet for at frygte stigmaet. Studiet interviewede 20 amerikanske forskere om deres erfaringer og viser, at vidensdelingen mellem videnskab og godkendelsesmyndigheder ikke bare er hjælpsom—det er væsentligt.

items.title: Mechanisms involved in the sex-dependent dopaminergic neurodegeneration induced by MDMA in a mouse model of adolescent drug exposure

summaries.en:
Here's a striking finding: MDMA affects male and female adolescent brains differently. Researchers gave young mice a dose of MDMA and discovered that the damage to a key dopamine-producing brain region (crucial for movement and motivation) unfolded differently depending on sex—revealing that biology matters when it comes to drug toxicity. This matters because adolescence is when the brain is still developing, and understanding these sex-specific risks could help us better protect young people.

Scientists tracked what happens in the brain at different time points after MDMA exposure, measuring antioxidant defenses, inflammation, and cell damage markers. The work zooms in on the molecular mechanisms driving MDMA's harmful effects—exactly the kind of detailed mechanistic research that's pushing psychedelic science forward. As researchers explore both the therapeutic potential and safety profiles of psychedelics, studies like this remind us why rigorous, nuanced science matters: it keeps the conversation honest and grounded.
summaries.da:
Her er et slående fund: MDMA påvirker mandlige og kvindelige adolescentes hjerner forskelligt. Forskere gav unge mus en dosis MDMA og opdagede, at skaden på en vigtig dopamin-producerende hjernedel (afgørende for bevægelse og motivation) forløb sig forskelligt afhængigt af køn—og viser, at biologi betyder noget for stoffets giftighed. Det betyder noget, fordi puberteten er når hjernen stadig udvikler sig, og at forstå disse kønsspecifikke risici kan hjælpe os med bedre at beskytte unge mennesker.

Forskerne fulgte, hvad der sker i hjernen på forskellige tidspunkter efter MDMA-eksponering og målte antioxidant-forsvaret, betændelse og celleskadesmarkører. Arbejdet zoomer ind på de molekylære mekanismer bag MDMAs skadelige effekter—præcis den slags detaljeret mekanistisk forskning, der driver psykedelika-forskningen fremad. Mens forskere udforsker både det terapeutiske potentiale og sikkerhedsprofilen af psykedelika, minder studier som dette os om, hvorfor stringent, nuanceret videnskab betyder noget: det holder samtalen ærlig og jordnær.

items.title: Beyond self, time, and space: exceptional experiences and altered states of consciousness

summaries.en:
Ever felt like you knew something before it happened? Or experienced a moment that felt cosmically meaningful? These aren't just personal quirks—they're widespread across cultures, and science is taking them seriously. New research explores how exceptional experiences like precognition and meaningful coincidences might reveal something profound about consciousness itself, especially when they happen during altered states like meditation or psychedelic trips.

The challenge? Most of these experiences occur in deeply personal, emotionally charged moments that labs can't easily recreate. Researchers are now combining traditional experiments with qualitative methods—actually listening to people's stories—to understand these phenomena better. As psychedelics move into mainstream research, studying how they unlock these exceptional experiences could reshape our understanding of what consciousness really is.
summaries.da:
Har du nogensinde haft en følelse af at vide noget før det skete? Eller oplevet et øjeblik, der føltes kosmisk meningsfuldt? Det er ikke bare personlige særheder—det er udbredt på tværs af kulturer, og videnskaben tager det alvorligt. Ny forskning udforsker, hvordan ekstraordinære oplevelser som præmonitioner og meningsfulde tilfældigheder kunne afsløre noget dybt om bevidstheden, især når de opstår under forandrede bevidsthedstilstande som meditation eller psykedelika-oplevelser.

Udfordringen? De fleste af disse oplevelser opstår i dybt personlige, følelsesmæssigt ladede øjeblikke, som laboratorier ikke let kan efterligne. Forskere kombinerer nu traditionelle eksperimenter med kvalitative metoder—faktisk at høre på menneskers historier—for at forstå disse fænomener bedre. Mens psykedelika moves ind i mainstream-forskning, kunne at studere hvordan de åbner disse ekstraordinære oplevelser omforme vores forståelse af hvad bevidsthed egentlig er.

items.title: Ketamine, an interoceptive associative agent? Evidence from ketamine-assisted Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement for opioid use disorder.

summaries.en: Here's something striking: people struggling with opioid addiction who received ketamine alongside mindfulness training showed a rapid boost in body awareness—noticing their own physical sensations more clearly—and this shift directly helped reduce their cravings. Researchers think ketamine might act like a bridge, rewiring how the brain processes internal signals so that mindfulness practice can take deeper root. This secondary analysis of 68 adults on buprenorphine compared eight weeks of mindfulness-based recovery training with and without ketamine assistance, tracking real-time body awareness and cravings. The results suggest we're looking at a genuinely new mechanism: psychedelics may not just shift consciousness, they might retrain our relationship with our own bodies—something addiction actively disrupts. It's a clue pointing toward how ketamine could amplify therapy in ways we're only beginning to understand.
summaries.da: Her er noget markant: mennesker, der kæmper med opioidafhængighed og fik psykedelika sammen med mindfulness-træning, oplevede et hurtigt løft i kropsbevidsthed—de mærkede deres egne fysiske fornemmelser tydeligere—og denne skift reducerede direkte deres trang. Forskerne tror, at psykedelika kunne fungere som en bro, der gentelegrer hjernens behandling af indre signaler, så mindfulness-praksis kan få dybere rod. Denne analyse af 68 voksne sammenlignet otte uger med mindfulness-baseret genopretningsprogrammet med og uden psykedelika, og fulgte deres kropsbevidsthed og trang i realtid. Resultaterne tyder på, at vi ser en genuint ny mekanisme: psykedelika omkabler måske ikke bare bevidstheden, de træner vores forhold til vores egne kroppe—noget afhængighed aktivt ødelægger. Det er en ledetråd, der peger mod, hvordan psykedelika kunne forstærke terapi på måder, vi kun lige begynder at forstå.

items.title: Intravenous Ketamine or Esketamine in Adolescents With Major Depressive Disorder: A Systematic Review.

summaries.en:
Teen depression might respond to esketamine—a form of ketamine—better than we thought, but we're only starting to understand how. A new review of three small clinical trials found that intravenous esketamine showed real promise for reducing depression and even suicidal thoughts in adolescents, something that standard ketamine didn't consistently achieve. The catch? Both forms caused dissociative experiences (feeling detached from your body or surroundings), and esketamine triggered more psychological side effects—raising real questions about what's worth tolerating.

Here's what makes this important: depression in teens is serious, and current treatments don't work for everyone. Researchers gave adolescents these substances under controlled medical conditions to see what happened. The evidence is still sparse and messy—only three studies, small groups, and gaps in how side effects were reported—but it hints that psychedelics like esketamine could eventually offer new hope for young people in real crisis. We're nowhere near recommending this as routine treatment, but the direction of the science is worth watching closely.
summaries.da:
Teenage depression kunne måske reagere bedre på esketamin—en form af ketamin—end vi troede, men vi er kun ved at forstå hvordan. En ny gennemgang af tre små kliniske forsøg viste, at intravenøs esketamin havde stort løfte til at reducere depression og selv selvmordstanker hos unge, noget som standard ketamin ikke konsekvent præsterede. Men der er en pris: begge former forårsagede dissociative oplevelser (følelse af at være løsrevet fra kroppen eller omgivelserne), og esketamin udløste flere psykologiske bivirkninger—hvilket rejser rigtige spørgsmål om, hvad det er værd at tåle.

Her er, hvorfor det betyder noget: depression hos unge er alvorlig, og nuværende behandlinger virker ikke for alle. Forskere gav unge mennesker disse stoffer under kontrollerede medicinske forhold for at se, hvad der skete. Beviserne er stadig sparsomme og rodet—kun tre studier, små grupper og huller i, hvordan bivirkninger blev rapporteret—men det antyder, at psykedelika som esketamin måske kunne give håb til unge mennesker i virkelig krise. Vi er langt fra at anbefale det som rutinemæssig behandling, men retningen af videnskaben er værd at følge nøje.

items.title: Integrating multi-receptor and neuron-glia mechanisms of ketamine's antidepressant action: a convergence framework for understanding efficacy.

summaries.en:
Ketamine works fast against depression—sometimes within hours—but scientists have been puzzled about exactly how. New research reveals it's not just one mechanism at play: ketamine simultaneously flips switches across multiple receptor systems in the brain, from glutamate signaling to growth factors, while also recruiting immune cells called glia to support the process. This explains why it's so effective where traditional antidepressants often fail.

Researchers combined decades of findings into a unified model showing how ketamine's various effects converge to rewire depressed brains. This matters because it moves us beyond simplistic explanations and opens doors to designing better, faster-acting treatments—and potentially understanding how other psychedelics might work similarly. We're watching psychiatry shift from treating symptoms to actually understanding the biology beneath depression.
summaries.da:
Ketamin virker hurtigt mod depression—nogle gange inden for timer—men forskere har længe været forundret over præcis hvordan. Ny forskning viser at det ikke blot er én mekanisme: ketamin aktiverer samtidigt flere systemer i hjernen, fra glutamat-signalering til vækststoffer, og rekrutterer samtidig immunceller kaldet glia til at støtte processen. Det forklarer hvorfor det virker hvor traditionelle antidepressiva ofte fejler.

Forskere har kombineret årtiers resultater til en samlet model, der viser hvordan ketamins forskellige effekter konvergerer og omkoder deprimerede hjerner. Det betyder noget fordi det flytter os bort fra simple forklaringer og åbner døre til bedre, hurtigere virkende behandlinger—og potentielt forståelse af hvordan andre psykedelika måske virker på samme måde. Vi ser psykiatrien skifte fra at behandle symptomer til faktisk at forstå biologien bag depression.

items.title: Intermittent theta burst stimulation to extend early ketamine response in treatment-resistant depression: A preliminary enriched randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.

summaries.en: Ketamine works fast for depression—but the relief fades within days. New research shows that combining it with a non-invasive brain stimulation technique called theta-burst stimulation might extend that benefit. In a trial with people who hadn't responded to other treatments, those who received five days of this stimulation after ketamine maintained their improvements better than those who didn't. Scientists also spotted changes in how different brain regions connected to each other. While the results are promising, they're still early-stage—but they hint at a practical way to make ketamine's rapid-onset effects stick around longer.
summaries.da: Ketamin virker hurtigt mod depression—men lettelsen forsvinder inden for få dage. Ny forskning viser, at det at kombinere det med en ikke-invasiv hjernestimulationsteknik kaldet theta-burst-stimulation måske kan forlænge effekten. I et forsøg med mennesker, der ikke havde reageret på andre behandlinger, bibeholdt de, der fik fem dages stimulation efter ketamin, deres forbedringer bedre end de andre. Forskerne opdagede også ændringer i, hvordan forskellige hjerneregiactualoner forbandt sig til hinanden. Resultaterne er lovende, men stadig i en tidlig fase—men de peger på en praktisk måde at få ketamins hurtige virkning til at vare længere.

items.title: From Toad Venom to Drug Development: The Clinical Pharmacology of Mebufotenin (5-MeO-DMT) in Treatment-Resistant Depression.

summaries.en: One in three people with depression don't respond to standard medication—and researchers are now exploring an unexpected solution: a compound from toad venom and Amazonian plants called mebufotenin (5-MeO-DMT). Early evidence suggests this psychedelic could help where conventional drugs fail, offering real hope for treatment-resistant depression. Scientists conducted a comprehensive review of mebufotenin's pharmacology and clinical development to understand how it works in the brain and body. This research fits into a broader shift: psychedelics are moving from fringe curiosity to serious pharmaceutical development, with multiple trials now investigating how these compounds might unlock new pathways for people who've exhausted other options. It's a reminder that sometimes healing comes from unexpected places.
summaries.da: En af tre mennesker med depression reagerer ikke på almindelig medicin—og forskere udforsker nu en usandsynlig løsning: et stof fra tudekryller og amazonske planter kaldet mebufotenin (5-MeO-DMT). Tidlige tegn tyder på, at dette psykedelikum kunne hjælpe dér, hvor konventionelle lægemidler svigter, og giver håb til mennesker med behandlingsresistent depression. Forskere gennemgik omhyggeligt mebufotenins farmakologi og kliniske udvikling for at forstå, hvordan det virker i hjerne og krop. Denne forskning passer ind i en større forandring: psykedelika bevæger sig fra marginalt kuriøsitet til seriøs lægemiddelacceleration, hvor flere forsøg nu udforsker, hvordan disse stoffer kan åbne nye veje for mennesker, der har udtømt andre muligheder. Det minder os om, at healing nogle gange kommer fra uventede steder.

items.title: Exploring the durability of esketamine and ketamine's antidepressant effects in the maintenance phase of treatment: A systematic review.

summaries.en: Ketamine works fast for depression that won't respond to other treatments — but here's the crucial question: does the magic last? A new review of 43 studies reveals that yes, the benefits stick around *if you keep taking it*. But stop treatment, and relapse often follows. The research shows repeated ketamine and esketamine doses maintain improvement during ongoing care, though results vary depending on how the studies were designed. This matters because it shifts how we think about ketamine: not as a quick fix, but as a maintenance therapy that may need to continue over time. As psychedelics move from breakthrough hype into real clinical practice, understanding what *durability* actually looks like — the unglamorous but essential question of 'does this actually work long-term?' — is exactly the kind of grounded science that will shape how these tools get used in hospitals and clinics.
summaries.da: Ketamin virker hurtigt på depression, som andre behandlinger ikke kan løse — men her er det afgørende spørgsmål: holder magien ved? Et nyt overblik over 43 studier afslører, at ja, effekten bliver ved *hvis du bliver ved med at tage det*. Men stop behandlingen, og tilbagefald følger ofte. Forskningen viser, at gentagne doser ketamin og esketamin opretholder forbedring under løbende behandling, selvom resultaterne varierer afhængigt af, hvordan studierne var designet. Det betyder noget, fordi det ændrer, hvordan vi tænker på ketamin: ikke som en lynløsning, men som en vedligeholdelsesterapi, der muligvis skal fortsætte over tid. Når psykedelika bevæger sig fra revolutionær hype hen imod virkelig klinisk praksis, er det præcis denne jordnære forskning — det usexy men væsentlige spørgsmål 'virker det faktisk længere tid?' — der skal forme, hvordan disse værktøjer bruges på hospitaler og klinikker.

items.title: Next-Generation Psychedelic Drug Development.

summaries.en: Depression, anxiety, PTSD—psychedelics are showing real promise for treating conditions that have resisted traditional medicine for decades. But as researchers race to develop next-generation versions of these compounds, we're hitting an important moment: which approaches actually work, and how do we know? A new review digs into the science behind novel psychedelics and the tools we use to test them, laying bare what's working brilliantly and where we're still flying somewhat blind. This matters because psychedelic research is moving fast—new molecules, new protocols, new possibilities—and getting the fundamentals right now could shape the entire field for years to come.
summaries.da: Depression, angst, PTSD—psykedelika viser rigtig potentiale for at behandle tilstande, som traditionel medicin har kæmpet med i årtier. Men mens forskere løber af sted med at udvikle næste generations udgaver af disse stoffer, står vi over for et afgørende øjeblik: hvilke tilgange virker egentlig, og hvordan ved vi det? En ny gennemgang dykker ned i videnskaben bag nye psykedelika og de værktøjer, vi bruger til at teste dem, og blotlægger både hvad der virker glimrende og hvor vi stadig er ret uklare. Det betyder noget, fordi psykedelika-forskningen bevæger sig hurtigt—nye molekyler, nye protokoller, nye muligheder—og at få grundlaget på plads nu kunne præge hele feltet i mange år fremover.

items.title: Ketamine/Esketamine in Clinical Practice: Areas of Consensus and Nonconsensus from an American Society of Clinical Psychopharmacology (ASCP) Delphi Panel Task Force.

summaries.en:
Ketamine is becoming a real option for people with severe depression and suicidal thoughts — but experts still disagree on the best way to use it. A major panel of American clinical psychopharmacologists gathered to figure out where they actually agree on ketamine and esketamine in practice, and where the questions still linger. It turns out there's solid consensus on some things (it works fast, it can help when other treatments fail), but plenty of debate remains about dosing, how often people should receive it, and what happens after treatment stops.

This kind of expert consensus-building matters because ketamine represents something genuinely new in how we treat severe mental health crises — it works differently than traditional antidepressants and can offer relief within hours rather than weeks. As the psychedelic research field expands into examining how these compounds might heal the mind, understanding exactly how to use existing tools like ketamine in clinical settings becomes crucial. The honest disagreements documented here actually show the field taking itself seriously: there's real science happening, not hype.
summaries.da:
Ketamin bliver et reelt håb for mennesker med svær depression og selvmordstanker — men eksperter er stadig uenige om den bedste måde at bruge det på. Et stort panel af amerikanske kliniske psykofarmakologer mødte for at finde ud af, hvor de faktisk er enige om ketamin og esketamin i praksis, og hvor spørgsmålene stadig hænger i luften. Det viser sig, at der er solid enighed om nogle ting (det virker hurtigt, det kan hjælpe når andre behandlinger fejler), men der er rigelig debat om dosering, hvor ofte mennesker skal have det, og hvad der sker efter behandlingen slutter.

Denne slags ekspertkonsensus betyder noget, fordi ketamin repræsenterer noget virkelig nyt i hvordan vi behandler alvorlige psykiske kriser — det virker anderledes end traditionelle antidepressiva og kan give lindring indenfor timer i stedet for uger. Når psykedelika-forskningsfeltet udvider sig til at undersøge hvordan disse stoffer kan helbrede sindet, bliver det afgørende at forstå præcis hvordan man bruger eksisterende værktøjer som ketamin klinisk. De ærlige uenigheder dokumenteret her viser faktisk, at feltet tager sig selv seriøst: der sker rigtig videnskab, ikke hype.

items.title: Bridging Nonconsecutive Esketamine Weeks with Bupropion and Over-the-Counter Dextromethorphan.

summaries.en: A woman with severe depression that hadn't responded to other treatments found her symptoms would crash within just 10 days if she missed her weekly esketamine clinic visits—her depression score could spike from near-remission to severe in a single delayed appointment. But here's what's interesting: by combining two other medicines (an over-the-counter cough suppressant and an antidepressant) between esketamine sessions, she managed to stretch treatments to every other week without relapsing. Researchers think the two drugs work on similar brain pathways, and one helps keep the other at stable levels in her body. This case study hints at something bigger: as psychedelics move into mainstream medicine, the logistics of getting people to frequent clinic visits is a real barrier. These early findings suggest we might develop smart combinations that make psychedelic treatments more practical and accessible—though much more research is needed to know if this approach works for others.
summaries.da: En kvinde med alvorlig depression, der ikke reagerede på andre behandlinger, oplevede at hendes symptomer styrtdykkede inden for blot 10 dage, hvis hun missede hendes ugentlige esketamin-klinikbesøg—hendes depressionsscore kunne stige fra næsten fuldstændig remission til alvorlig tilstand ved en enkelt forsinket time. Men her er det interessante: ved at kombinere to andre mediciner (et håndkøbsmiddel mod hoste og et antidepressivum) mellem esketamin-behandlingerne lykkedes det hende at strække behandlingerne til hver anden uge uden tilbagefald. Forskere tror, at de to stoffer virker på lignende hjernebaner, og det ene hjælper med at holde det andet på stabilt niveau i kroppen. Denne case study antyder noget større: når psykedelika bevæger sig ind i mainstream medicin, er logistikken omkring hyppige klinikbesøg en reel barriere. Disse tidlige resultater tyder på, at vi måske kan udvikle smarte kombinationer, der gør psykedelika-behandlinger mere praktiske og tilgængelige—selvom meget mere forskning er nødvendig for at vide, om denne fremgangsmåde virker for andre.

items.title: Potent and Irreversible? Evaluating the In Vitro Monoamine Oxidase Inhibition Potential of Eight Psychedelics of the Cyclopropylamine Type

summaries.en: Scientists just tested eight psychedelics to see if they could dangerously interfere with how your brain breaks down mood-regulating chemicals. The good news? Most of them—including 25D-CPA, a compound chemically similar to an old psychiatric drug—showed surprisingly weak effects compared to what researchers feared. This matters because if psychedelics messed too much with these brain processes, it could cause serious problems. Researchers used lab-grown enzymes and advanced chemical analysis to measure exactly how much each psychedelic blocked these processes. This kind of detailed safety work is exactly what the field needs right now: as psychedelics move toward real clinical use, we need to understand not just whether they help people, but exactly how they work and what risks they carry. One study doesn't settle everything, but it's a solid piece of the puzzle.
summaries.da: Forskere har netop testet otte psykedelika for at se, om de farligt kunne blande sig ind i, hvordan din hjerne nedbryder stemningsregulerende kemikalier. Det gode nyt? De fleste af dem—herunder 25D-CPA, en forbindelse der ligner et gammelt psykiatrisk lægemiddel—viste overraskende svage effekter sammenlignet med det, forskerne frygtede. Det betyder noget, fordi hvis psykedelika blokerede for meget af disse hjerneprocesrer, kunne det forårsage alvorlige problemer. Forskerne brugte laboratorieenzymer og avanceret kemisk analyse til at måle præcis, hvor meget hvert psykedelikum blokerede disse processer. Præcis denne slags sikkerhedsarbejde er netop hvad området har brug for nu: når psykedelika bevæger sig mod faktisk klinisk brug, skal vi forstå ikke blot om de hjælper mennesker, men præcis hvordan de virker og hvilke risici de bærer. Én undersøgelse afgør ikke alt, men det er et solidt puslespilsbrik.

items.title: From Evidence to Practice: A Systematic Review of Implementation of Psychedelic-Assisted Psychotherapy.

summaries.en: We know psychedelics can help people with trauma, depression, and other tough mental health struggles—the science is clear. But here's the catch: getting these treatments from the lab into actual clinics where patients need them is a whole different challenge. A new systematic review looked at everything we currently know about implementing psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy in real-world settings, examining six databases to find what actually works when it comes to rolling out these complex treatments. The findings matter because there's often a huge gap between discovering that something works and actually making it available to people. As psychedelics move closer to becoming approved treatments in more countries, understanding the practical hurdles—training therapists, setting up clinics, getting funding—becomes crucial. This review maps out what we know so far and what still needs figuring out, helping pave the way for smarter, more systematic implementation that could get help to people faster.
summaries.da: Vi ved, at psykedelika kan hjælpe mennesker med traume, depression og andre svære psykiske lidelser—videnskaben er klar. Men her er kniben: at få disse behandlinger fra laboratoriet ind i rigtige klinikker, hvor patienter har brug for dem, er en helt anden udfordring. Et nyt systematisk review kiggede på alt, hvad vi i øjeblikket ved om implementeringen af psykedelika-assisteret psykoterapi i praksis, og undersøgte seks databaser for at finde ud af, hvad der fungerer, når det handler om at få disse komplekse behandlinger i gang. Fundet betyder noget, fordi der ofte er et enormt hul mellem at opdage, at noget virker, og faktisk at gøre det tilgængeligt for mennesker. Når psykedelika kommer tættere på at blive godkendt som behandlinger i flere lande, bliver det afgørende at forstå de praktiske forhindringer—uddannelse af terapeuter, etablering af klinikker, finansiering. Dette review kortlægger, hvad vi ved i dag, og hvad der stadig skal undersøges, og hjælper dermed med at forberede vejen for smartere og mere systematisk implementering.

items.title: Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy for Cancer-Related Psychological and Existential Distress in Adults with Cancer: An Integrative Systematic Review.

summaries.en: Imagine facing a cancer diagnosis and finding that a single guided session with psilocybin could ease your depression, anxiety, and fear of death—sometimes for years. That's what this major review of six clinical studies found: people with cancer experienced rapid, lasting relief from psychological distress, with many reporting newfound acceptance, spiritual clarity, and a reconnection with what makes life meaningful. Researchers gave participants one moderate-to-high dose in a carefully structured setting and tracked outcomes over months and even years. The findings matter because they show psychedelics aren't just recreating earlier counterculture experiments—they're becoming a serious tool for end-of-life care and mental health support. As cancer therapies improve and people live longer with their diagnosis, this research points to a compassionate way to address the existential weight that often comes with the disease.
summaries.da: Forestil dig at få diagnosen cancer og så opdage, at en enkelt guidet session med psykedelika kunne lette din depression, angst og dødsangst—nogle gange i år efter. Det er netop hvad denne omfattende gennemgang af seks kliniske studier viste: mennesker med cancer oplevede hurtig, varig lindring af psykisk belastning, og mange rapporterede øget accept, spirituel klarhed og en ny forbindelse til det, som gør livet meningsfuldt. Forskerne gav deltagerne én moderat-høj dosis i et omhyggeligt struktureret miljø og fulgte resultaterne over måneder og sågar år. Resultaterne betyder noget, fordi de viser, at psykedelika ikke blot genskaber gamle eksperimenter—de bliver et seriøst værktøj for palliativ omsorg og mental sundhed. Efterhånden som cancerbehandlinger forbedres og mennesker lever længere med deres diagnose, peger denne forskning på en medfølende måde at håndtere den eksistentielle vægt, som ofte følger med sygdommen.

items.title: Compass Says NDA Will Be Filed Within Two Weeks, Declines to Comment on Usona

summaries.en: We're inches away from a major milestone: Compass Pathways is filing its FDA application for COMP360, a psilocybin treatment for treatment-resistant depression, within the next two weeks. This isn't just corporate news—it's a sign that psychedelics are moving from underground experiments into the regulated medical system, potentially offering hope to people whose depression hasn't responded to anything else. The company shared this update in their latest quarterly results, marking real progress on a path that started years ago in research labs. This NDA filing represents a crucial moment for the whole field: if approved, it would be the first psilocybin therapy available by prescription, signalling to regulators, doctors, and patients that psychedelics deserve serious scientific consideration as medicine.
summaries.da: Vi er på vej mod et stort gennembrud: Compass Pathways indgiver ansøgning til FDA om COMP360, en psilocybin-behandling for behandlingsresistent depression, inden for de næste to uger. Det er ikke bare virksomhedsnyt—det viser, at psykedelika bevæger sig fra underground-eksperimenter ind i det regulerede medicinsystem, og kan potentielt give håb til mennesker, hvis depression ikke har reageret på noget andet. Virksomheden delte denne opdatering i deres seneste kvartalsresultater, hvilket markerer konkret fremskridt på en vej, der startede for år siden i forskningstilsamlingen. Denne NDA-indgivelse er et afgørende øjeblik for hele området: hvis det godkendes, ville det være den første psilocybin-terapi tilgængelig på recept, hvilket signalerer til tilsynsmyndigheder, læger og patienter, at psykedelika fortjener seriøs videnskabelig overvejelse som medicin.

items.title: Toxicological studies on the Inca frozen mummies from volcanoes in Peru and Argentina

summaries.en: Ancient Inca sacrifices reveal a stunning secret: they were given cocaine and other psychoactive substances before their final ritual journey to the mountain gods. Researchers analyzed hair and nail samples from eight frozen mummies found high in the Andes, uncovering traces of cocaine, cocaethylene, and harmine—substances the Inca used to prepare these individuals for their sacred role as messengers to the deities. This toxicological detective work shows us that psychedelics and other mind-altering plants played a central part in Inca spiritual practice, not as casual use but as deliberate preparation for profound, life-changing moments. The findings reveal how different regions of the Inca Empire had their own ritual variations, and they add a crucial piece to our understanding of how ancient cultures integrated psychoactive substances into their worldview. As modern research explores psychedelics' potential for healing and spiritual insight, these 500-year-old mummies remind us that humans have always sought these substances for transformation—and that understanding this deep history matters.
summaries.da: Gamle inkaofre afslører en forbløffende hemmelighed: de fik kokain og andre psykoaktive stoffer før deres sidste rituelle rejse til bjergeguderne. Forskere analyserede hår- og neglprøver fra otte frosne mumier fundet højt oppe i Anderne og opdagede spor af kokain, cocaethylen og harmin—stoffer som inkaerne brugte til at forberede disse mennesker til deres hellige rolle som budbringere til guderne. Dette toksikologiske detektivarbejde viser os, at psykedelika og andre sindsomdannende planter spillede en central rolle i inkaernes spirituelle praksis, ikke som tilfældig brug men som bevidst forberedelse til dybe, livsforandrende øjeblikke. Fundet afslører, hvordan forskellige dele af inkaeriget havde deres egen rituelle variation, og det tilføjer et afgørende puslespil til vores forståelse af, hvordan gamle kulturer integrerede psykoaktive stoffer i deres verdensopfattelse. Mens moderne forskning udforsker psykedelikas potentiale for helbredelse og åndelig indsigt, minder disse 500 år gamle mumier os om, at mennesker altid har søgt disse stoffer for transformation—og at det betyder noget at forstå denne dybe historie.

items.title: Mechanism-guided generative chemistry yields distinct agonist-like and antagonist-like ligand populations for the serotonin 5-HT2A receptor

summaries.en:
Scientists just cracked a major puzzle in psychedelic chemistry: how to design molecules that reliably act as either agonists or antagonists at the 5-HT2A receptor—the key player in how psychedelics affect your brain. This matters because it's been notoriously hard to predict whether a molecule will activate or block this receptor, even when you know it binds to it. Using AI-powered generative chemistry, researchers created 500 distinct agonist-like candidates and 500 antagonist-like ones, mapping out the structural differences that make each type tick.

The team combined machine learning with molecular docking and chemistry expertise to guide the AI's design process, training on nearly 9,000 existing measurements. This breakthrough doesn't just solve a technical headache—it opens the door to smarter, more targeted psychedelic drug development. As research shifts from asking "do psychedelics work?" to "how do we make better ones?", this kind of precision tool becomes essential. It's the kind of foundational work that might eventually help researchers fine-tune therapies for depression, anxiety, and beyond.
summaries.da:
Forskere har lige løst et stort puslespil inden for psykedelika-kemi: hvordan designer man molekyler, der pålideligt virker som enten agonister eller antagonister på 5-HT2A-receptoren—den vigtigste nøgle til, hvordan psykedelika påvirker din hjerne. Det betyder noget, fordi det hidtil har været enormt svært at forudsige, om et molekyle vil aktivere eller blokere denne receptor, selv når man ved, at det binder til den. Ved hjælp af AI-drevet kemigenerering skabte forskere 500 distinkte agonist-lignende kandidater og 500 antagonist-lignende, og kortlagde de strukturelle forskelle, der gør hver type unik.

Teamet kombinerede maskinlæring med molekylær docking og kemisk ekspertise for at guide AI'ens designproces, trænet på næsten 9.000 eksisterende målinger. Dette gennembrud løser ikke bare et teknisk problem—det åbner døren til mere målrettet psykedelika-lægemiddelsforskning. Mens forskningen skifter fra at spørge "virker psykedelika?" til "hvordan laver vi bedre?" bliver denne præcisionsværktøj vigtig. Det er grundlæggende arbejde, der måske engang hjælper forskere med at finjustere terapier mod depression, angst og mere til.

items.title: A multi-institutional investigation of psilocybin's effects on mouse behavior.

summaries.en:
Here's something scientists rarely talk about: most psychedelic studies on animals haven't been tested to see if they actually work the same way twice. Five independent labs just ran identical psilocybin experiments on mice to find out which effects are real and which might just be flukes. The result? Some behavioral changes held up across every single lab, while others disappeared—a crucial reality check for the field.

This kind of rigorous replication work might sound boring, but it's foundational. As psychedelic research scales up toward human clinical trials, we need to know exactly which animal findings we can trust. This study is like sharpening the tools before building the house—it's helping the whole field move forward with confidence and precision.
summaries.da:
Her er noget forskerne sjældent taler om: de fleste psykedelika-studier på dyr er aldrig blevet testet for at se, om de virker på samme måde to gange. Fem uafhængige laboratorier har netop kørt identiske psilocybin-eksperimenter på mus for at finde ud af, hvilke adfærdsændringer der er rigtige, og hvilke der måske bare er tilfældigheder. Resultatet? Nogle effekter holdt sig konsistent på tværs af hvert eneste lab, mens andre forsvandt—en afgørende virkelightstjek for feltet.

Denne type grundig replikationsforskning lyder måske kedelig, men den er fundamental. Når psykedelika-forskningen skaleres op mod menneskelige kliniske forsøg, skal vi vide præcis hvilke dyrefund vi kan stole på. Dette studie er som at slibe værktøjerne inden man bygger huset—det hjælper hele feltet fremad med tillid og præcision.

items.title: Effects of psilocybin with psychological support on anhedonia in treatment-resistant depression: A randomized controlled pilot trial

summaries.en:
Imagine feeling nothing—no joy, no motivation, no spark. That's anhedonia, and it's devastating people with treatment-resistant depression who've exhausted traditional options. A new pilot study tested whether psilocybin, paired with psychological support, could restore that lost ability to feel pleasure. Early results are intriguing enough that researchers are digging deeper into how this psychedelic might rewire the brain's reward system in ways antidepressants alone haven't managed.

The study followed a randomized controlled design—the gold standard for testing whether something actually works. What's exciting is how this fits into a broader shift in mental health research: psychedelics aren't a magic bullet, but combined with therapy, they're revealing unexpected pathways to healing stubborn depression. We're witnessing science take seriously what many people have long suspected: sometimes the most stuck problems need the most unconventional solutions.
summaries.da:
Forestil dig at føle intet—ingen glæde, ingen motivation, ingen gnist. Det er anhedoni, og det ødelægger livet for mennesker med behandlingsresistent depression, som har prøvet alt traditionelt. Et nyt pilotforsøg testede, om psilocybin kombineret med psykologisk støtte kunne genoplive evnen til at føle nydelse. De indledende resultater er spændende nok til, at forskere graver dybere ned i, hvordan dette psykedelikum kunne omskabe hiernens belønningssystem på måder, som antidepressiva alene ikke har formået.

Studiet fulgte et randomiseret kontrolleret design—guldstandarden for at teste, om noget virkeligt virker. Det spændende er, hvordan dette passer ind i et større skift inden for psykisk sundhedsforskning: psykedelika er ikke en universalmedicin, men kombineret med terapi åbner de uventede veje til helbredelse af håbløs depression. Vi er vidner til videnskab, der tager alvorligt, hvad mange længe har været overbevist om: nogle gange kræver de mest fastlåste problemer de mest ukonventionelle løsninger.

items.title: A multi-institutional investigation of psilocybin’s effects on mouse behavior

summaries.en: Five labs across multiple institutions just ran the same psilocybin experiment on mice to figure out what actually works—and the results are surprisingly humbling. The psychedelic boosted anxiety-related behaviors and reduced fear in the moment, which is interesting, but here's the catch: those lasting therapeutic effects everyone talks about? They didn't show up 24 hours later in a reliable way. No consistent help with anxiety, depression, or fear learning when they measured it days out. This matters because psychedelic research is moving fast, with exciting clinical trials happening in humans right now. This rigorous multi-lab study is exactly the kind of reality-check science needs: it pins down what actually replicates and what doesn't, helping researchers design better studies and manage expectations as we work toward real treatments.
summaries.da: Fem laboratorier på tværs af flere institutioner gennemførte netop det samme psykedelika-eksperiment på mus for at finde ud af, hvad der virkeligt virker—og resultaterne er overraskende ydmygende. Psilocybin øgede angstrelerede adfærd og reducerede frygt i øjeblikket, hvilket er interessant, men her kommer ketchuppet: de vedvarende terapeutiske effekter, som alle snakker om? De dukkede ikke pålideligt op 24 timer senere. Ingen konsistent hjælp til angst, depression eller frygtelæring, da de målte det dage senere. Det betyder noget, fordi psykedelika-forskningen går stærkt med spændende kliniske forsøg på mennesker lige nu. Dette grundige multi-lab-studie er præcis den slags virkeligheds-tjek, som videnskaben har brug for: det præciserer hvad der faktisk gentages, og hvad der ikke gør, og hjælper forskere med at designe bedre studier og håndtere forventninger mens vi arbejder mod rigtige behandlinger.

items.title: Making psychedelics researchable: science, medicine, and the social construction of legitimacy

summaries.en: Whether psychedelics get studied—and how—isn't just about the science. It's about power, politics, and money. A new analysis reveals how social forces shape what research happens at all: prohibition shut down decades of promising work, but today's "psychedelic renaissance" is reopening doors. Here's the catch: the research getting funded now tends to focus on things that are easy to measure, package, and sell—which might not be the same as what actually helps people most. Understanding this hidden architecture matters if we want psychedelic science to serve healing, not just markets.
summaries.da: Om psykedelika bliver forsket i—og hvordan—handler ikke kun om videnskaben. Det handler om magt, politik og penge. En ny analyse afslører hvordan sociale kræfter former hvad der overhovedet bliver forsket i: Prohibition lukkede ned for årtiers lovende arbejde, men dagens "psykedelika-renæssance" åbner dørene igen. Men der er en hage: den forskning der får finansiering i dag fokuserer ofte på det, der er let at måle, pakke og sælge—hvilket måske ikke er det samme som det, der hjælper mennesker mest. At forstå denne skjulte arkitektur betyder noget, hvis vi vil have psykedelika-videnskaben til at tjene helbredelse, ikke kun markeder.

items.title: The molecular and neurochemical basis of altered intrinsic neural timescales in major depressive disorder: a multimodal imaging-transcriptomic investigation of esketamine and sertraline treatment.

summaries.en: Depression literally changes how your brain processes information — and new research shows that both esketamine and sertraline can reverse this at a molecular level. Scientists discovered that people with depression have altered neural timescales in key brain regions involved in emotion and thinking, and both treatments helped reset these patterns. In this study, researchers used brain imaging and genetic analysis to map exactly how these medications work, comparing 41 people with depression to healthy controls. The findings matter because they bridge a critical gap: we finally have concrete evidence of *how* these drugs change brain function, not just that they do. This is exactly where psychedelic research is heading — moving beyond 'does it work?' to 'here's the actual mechanism,' paving the way for smarter, more targeted treatments.
summaries.da: Depression ændrer bogstaveligt talt, hvordan din hjerne behandler information — og ny forskning viser, at både esketamin og sertralin kan vende det ved på molekylært niveau. Forskere opdagede, at mennesker med depression har ændrede neurale tidsskalaer i vigtige hjerneregio­ner, der styrer følelser og tænkning, og begge behandlinger hjalp med at nulstille disse mønstre. I denne undersøgelse brugte videnskabsmænd hjerneafbildning og genetisk analyse til at kortlægge præcis, hvordan disse lægemidler virker, ved at sammenligne 41 mennesker med depression med raske kontroller. Fundet betyder noget, fordi det overbrygger et kritisk gab: vi har endelig konkrete beviser for *hvordan* disse stoffer ændrer hjernefunktion, ikke bare at de gør det. Det er præcis hvor psykedelika-forskningen bevæger sig hen — bort fra 'virker det?' til 'her er den faktiske mekanisme,' hvilket baner vej for smartere, mere målrettede behandlinger.

items.title: Persisting psychological complications following the use of classic psychedelics: A qualitative study of help-seeking experiences.

summaries.en: Some people who use psychedelics experience lasting complications like visual disturbances, anxiety, or depersonalization—yet most doctors have no idea how to help them. A new study of 13 people living with these persistent effects reveals why: they're caught between hype that downplays risks and medical systems that dismiss their struggles as impossible. Many suffered in silence, blaming themselves, before finding support in online communities where others actually understood. The research, based on in-depth interviews, shows how media narratives and stigma shape the whole journey—from why people try psychedelics in the first place to why they struggle to get help afterward. When people did find clinicians who took them seriously and had real expertise, it made all the difference. As psychedelic research explodes, this study is an important reminder: we need honest conversations about both benefits and risks, and we urgently need medical professionals trained to support those who experience harm.
summaries.da: Nogle mennesker oplever varige komplikationer efter at have brugt psykedelika—visuelle forstyrrelser, angst eller depersonalisering—men de fleste læger ved slet ikke, hvordan de skal hjælpe dem. En ny dansk-relevant forskning med 13 personer, der lever med disse vedvarende effekter, afsløringer hvorfor: de er fanget mellem hype, der bagatelliserer risici, og medicinske systemer, der afviser deres kamp som umulig. Mange led i stilhed og beskyldte sig selv, før de fandt støtte i online-fællesskaber, hvor andre faktisk forstod dem. Undersøgelsen, baseret på dybdegående interviews, viser, hvordan medienarrativ og stigma påvirker hele rejsen—fra hvorfor mennesker først prøver psykedelika til hvorfor de kæmper med at få hjælp bagefter. Når folk mødte klinikere, der tog dem alvorligt og havde reel ekspertise, gjorde det hele forskellen. Mens psykedelika-forskningen eksploderer, er denne studie en vigtig påmindelse: vi har brug for ærlige samtaler om både fordele og risici, og vi har desperat brug for læger uddannet til at støtte dem, der oplever skade.

items.title: Transcriptional profiling of antidepressant ketamine and electroconvulsive therapy treatment.

summaries.en:
When depression doesn't respond to regular antidepressants, ketamine and electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) can work like a reset button—but until now, we haven't really understood why. A new study looked at blood samples from people with treatment-resistant depression before and after ketamine infusions or ECT, searching for genetic clues about who gets better. Here's what stood out: the researchers spotted immune system signals that might predict whether ketamine will actually help you, suggesting our body's defences play a hidden role in depression recovery.

Scientists analyzed thousands of genes across 132 people using advanced network analysis, essentially mapping how genes talk to each other during treatment. While they didn't find a single "magic marker" that works for everyone, these immune fingerprints in your blood could eventually become the personalised tests we've been waiting for—letting doctors predict treatment success before you start. This research sits at the exciting frontier where psychedelics and neuroscience are moving: from asking "does this work?" to "why does it work for some people and not others?"
summaries.da:
Når depression ikke reagerer på almindelige antidepressiva, kan ketamin og elektrokonvulsiv terapi (ECT) virke som en reset-knap—men indtil nu har vi ikke rigtig forstået hvorfor. Et nyt studie kiggede på blodprøver fra mennesker med behandlingsresistent depression før og efter ketamininfusioner eller ECT, på jagt efter genetiske spor om hvem der bliver bedre. Her er det slående: forskerne opdagede immunsystem-signaler, som kunne forudsige om ketamin faktisk hjælper dig, hvilket antyder at vores krops forsvar spiller en skjult rolle i depressionsgeneringen.

Videnskabsfolkene analyserede tusindvis af gener hos 132 mennesker ved hjælp af avanceret netværksanalyse, hvilket grundlæggende handler om at kortlægge hvordan gener taler med hinanden under behandling. Selvom de ikke fandt en enkelt "magisk markør" der virker for alle, kunne disse immunfingeraftryk i dit blod eventuelt blive de personliggørte tests vi har ventet på—som giver læger mulighed for at forudsige behandlingssucces før du starter. Denne forskning sidder på det spændende grænseland hvor psykedelika og neurovidenskab bevæger sig: fra at spørge "virker det?" til "hvorfor virker det for nogle mennesker og ikke andre?"

items.title: Podcast: Usona Files Psilocybin Application, We Review 610 Comments Submitted to FDA, and FDA Approves NRx’s Generic Ketamine

summaries.en:
Psychedelics just got a major regulatory push: Usona has filed for FDA approval of psilocybin as a depression treatment, and the FDA has already greenlit a generic version of ketamine. But here's what's really interesting—we reviewed 610 public comments submitted to the FDA, and they reveal what everyday people actually think about these medicines. The verdict? A lot of hope, mixed with real questions about access and safety.

This moment matters because it shows psychedelic research moving from lab curiosity into real-world policy. Researchers, patients, and regulators are all having the same conversation now, and the FDA is actually listening. We're watching the rules get written in real time—and that means understanding what people think about these treatments isn't just academic. It's shaping the future of mental healthcare.
summaries.da:
Psykedelika fik netop et stort fremskridt: Usona har indgivet ansøgning om FDA-godkendelse af psilocybin mod depression, og FDA har allerede godkendt en generisk version af ketamin. Men det mest interessante? Vi har gennemgået 610 offentlige kommentarer indsendt til FDA, og de afslører, hvad almindelige mennesker faktisk tænker om disse mediciner. Konklusionen er klar—masse håb blandet med reelle spørgsmål om tilgængelighed og sikkerhed.

Dette øjeblik betyder noget, fordi det viser psykedelikaforskning i færd med at blive reel politik, ikke blot laboratorieskepsis. Forskere, patienter og regulatorer har nu samme samtale, og FDA lytter faktisk til. Vi er vidne til, hvordan reglerne skrives lige nu—og det betyder, at forståelse af, hvad mennesker tænker om disse behandlinger, ikke bare er akademisk. Det former fremtiden for psykisk sundhedspleje.

items.title: Usona Files Psilocybin for Depression NDA as Race With Compass Tightens

summaries.en: We're watching history happen in real-time. Usona Institute just filed with the FDA to bring psilocybin to people struggling with severe depression—and it's only the second psychedelic compound ever to reach this stage. This means we're not just talking about potential anymore; regulators are seriously examining whether psychedelics could become legitimate medical treatments. Usona ran rigorous clinical trials to get here, and their move signals something bigger: we're in the middle of a genuine race to bring these molecules from underground to operating rooms. As more organizations push forward, the question isn't if psychedelics will transform mental healthcare—it's how quickly.
summaries.da: Vi er vidne til historie, der bliver skrevet lige nu. Usona Institute har netop indsendt ansøgning til FDA om at få psykedelika til mennesker, der kæmper med alvorlig depression—og det er kun det andet psykedeliske stof, der når til dette stadie. Det betyder, vi ikke længere bare taler om potentiale; regulatorer undersøger seriøst, om psykedelika kunne blive legitime medicinske behandlinger. Usona gennemførte strenge kliniske forsøg for at komme hertil, og deres skridt signalerer noget større: vi er midt i et ægte løb om at få disse molekyler fra underjorden til operationsstuer. Når flere organisationer fortsætter, handler spørgsmålet ikke længere om psykedelika vil transformere psykisk sundhed—det handler om hvor hurtigt det sker.

items.title: Furthering the Understanding of Psilocybin Use and Molecules Relevant to Depression and Schizophrenia

summaries.en: What if a single dose of psilocybin could help rewire the brain patterns that keep depression locked in place? New research is digging into exactly how psilocybin works at the molecular level, exploring connections that might also matter for schizophrenia. The findings suggest psychedelics don't just create a brief mystical experience—they may trigger deeper, lasting changes in how your brain processes emotion and meaning. Scientists analyzed psilocybin's effects on specific molecular pathways linked to depression and psychosis. This work is part of a bigger shift in psychiatry: moving from treating symptoms with daily pills to understanding whether a few carefully-guided psychedelic experiences could reset brain systems that have gone awry. We're still early, but the science keeps pointing toward something genuinely different.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis en enkelt dosis psilocybin kunne hjælpe med at omstille de hjernebaner, der holder depression på plads? Ny forskning dykker ned i præcis, hvordan psilocybin virker på molekylært niveau, og udforsker forbindelser, der måske også betyder noget for skizofreni. Fundet tyder på, at psykedelika ikke bare skaber en kort mystisk oplevelse—de kan udløse dybere, varige ændringer i, hvordan din hjerne behandler følelser og mening. Forskere analyserede psilocybins effekter på specifikke molekylære veje knyttet til depression og psykose. Dette arbejde er en del af et større skift inden for psykiatrien: væk fra at behandle symptomer med daglige piller, hen imod at forstå, om nogle få omhyggeligt vejledte psykedelika-oplevelser kunne nulstille hjernens systemer, der er gået i stykker. Vi er stadig tidligt inde, men videnskaben peger hele tiden på noget virkelig anderledes.

items.title: Psilocybin Use in Psychiatry: Clinical Practice and Public Health Implications.

summaries.en: Imagine a treatment that could help people with depression, anxiety, or PTSD in ways that traditional medicine sometimes can't—and without the side effects that come with many psychiatric drugs. New research is showing that psilocybin, the active compound in magic mushrooms, has real clinical potential in psychiatry. The evidence is compelling enough that doctors and researchers are seriously asking: how do we actually integrate this into mental healthcare? This isn't fringe thinking anymore—it's about figuring out the practical details of when, how, and for whom psychedelics should become part of standard treatment. As more clinical trials stack up, the conversation is shifting from "does this work?" to "how do we do this safely and responsibly?" That's where psychiatry is headed, and it could reshape mental health care for millions.
summaries.da: Forestil dig en behandling, der kunne hjælpe mennesker med depression, angst eller PTSD på måder, som traditionel medicin nogle gange ikke kan—uden de bivirkninger, som følger med mange psykiatriske lægemidler. Ny forskning viser, at psilocybin, det aktive stof i tryllehatte, har reel klinisk potentiale inden for psykiatri. Beviserne er så overbevisende, at læger og forskere stiller sig alvorligt spørgsmålet: hvordan integrerer vi dette egentlig i mental sundhedsvæsen? Dette er ikke længere kantsnak—det handler om at finde ud af de praktiske detaljer for hvornår, hvordan og for hvem psykedelika bør blive en del af standardbehandling. Efterhånden som flere kliniske forsøg ophober sig, skifter samtalen fra "virker det?" til "hvordan gør vi det sikkert og ansvarligt?" Det er retningen psykiatrien går, og det kunne omforme psykisk sundhedsvæsen for millioner af mennesker.

items.title: Therapeutic Potential of Classical Psychedelics and Non-Hallucinogenic Psychoplastogens in Psychiatric Disorders.

summaries.en: What if depression could shift in a single session instead of weeks on traditional pills? New research shows classical psychedelics like psilocybin and LSD can produce rapid mood improvements—sometimes lasting—when given with proper support. This builds on what ketamine taught us: that we don't need to wait months for antidepressants to kick in. Scientists reviewed the latest clinical evidence and identified real challenges ahead: studies are still small, it's hard to truly blind participants, and we need to separate genuine healing from placebo effects. But here's what matters: as psychedelic research moves from fringe to mainstream science, we're learning how these substances might reshape depression treatment—not as a quick fix, but as a potential tool for people who haven't found relief elsewhere.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis depression kunne skiftes på en enkelt session i stedet for uger på almindelige piller? Ny forskning viser, at klassiske psykedelika som psilocybin og LSD kan give hurtig stemningsforbedring—nogle gange varig—når de gives med ordentlig vejledning. Dette bygger på, hvad ketamin lærte os: at vi ikke skal vente måneder på, at antidepressiva virker. Forskere gennemgik de seneste kliniske beviser og identificerede rigtige udfordringer forude: studier er stadig små, det er svært at holde deltagere i mørke om hvad de får, og vi skal skelne ægte helbredelse fra placeboeffekter. Men her er det vigtige: mens psykedelika-forskning bevæger sig fra randzone til mainstream videnskab, lærer vi, hvordan disse stoffer kan omforme depressionbehandling—ikke som et hurtigt fix, men som et potentielt værktøj for mennesker, der ikke har fundet lindring andetsteds.

items.title: Furthering the Understanding of Psilocybin Use and Molecules Relevant to Depression and Schizophrenia.

summaries.en:
What if a single dose of psilocybin could reshape how our brains handle depression and psychosis? New research is diving into the molecular mechanics behind this possibility—exploring how psilocybin interacts with the brain systems that go awry in conditions like depression and schizophrenia. The findings are still emerging, but they're pointing toward something promising: psilocybin might work through entirely different pathways than the medications we've relied on for decades.

Scientists are systematically mapping out these molecular interactions to understand not just whether psilocybin helps, but exactly how and why. This detailed molecular understanding is becoming crucial as psychedelic research moves from the lab into clinical practice. By nailing down these mechanisms, researchers can develop safer treatments, predict who might benefit most, and potentially create new medicines inspired by psilocybin's effects. We're witnessing the foundation being laid for a genuinely new approach to mental health.
summaries.da:
Hvad hvis en enkelt dosis psilocybin kunne omforme, hvordan vores hjerner håndterer depression og psykose? Ny forskning dykker ned i de molekylære mekanismer bag denne mulighed—og udforsker, hvordan psilocybin interagerer med de hjernebaner, der går i stykker ved tilstande som depression og skizofreni. Fundet er stadig under udvikling, men det peger mod noget lovende: psilocybin arbejder måske gennem helt andre veje end de mediciner, vi har stole på i årtier.

Videnskabsmænd kortlægger systematisk disse molekylære interaktioner for at forstå ikke bare, om psilocybin hjælper, men præcis hvordan og hvorfor. Denne detaljerede molekylære forståelse bliver afgørende, når psykedelika-forskning går fra laboratoriet ind i klinisk praksis. Ved at få disse mekanismer på plads, kan forskere udvikle sikrere behandlinger, forudsige hvem der får mest gavn, og potentielt skabe nye mediciner inspireret af psilocybins effekter. Vi er vidner til, at der lægges grundlag for en virkelig ny tilgang til mental sundhed.

items.title: CARTOGRAFIA DAS EXPERIÊNCIAS COM A AYAHUASCA: MOTIVAÇÕES E MUDANÇAS NA COSMOVISÃO E NO ESTILO DE VIDA DE PRATICANTES DO SANTO DAIME NO AGRESTE PERNAMBUCANO

summaries.en: People who work with ayahuasca in the Santo Daime tradition report profound shifts in how they understand themselves, their relationships, and their place in the world. A new study following practitioners in northeastern Brazil found that the experience consistently sparked what participants described as deep care and existential reorganization—real changes in how they live and what matters to them. Researchers conducted interviews with six community members and embedded themselves in the tradition to map these experiences. The findings add an important piece to growing psychedelic research: traditional knowledge systems aren't just interesting historical artifacts, they're active approaches to healing and transformation that modern science is only beginning to understand properly.
summaries.da: Folk der arbejder med ayahuasca i Santo Daime-traditionen rapporterer om dybtgående skift i, hvordan de forstår sig selv, deres forhold og deres plads i verden. Et nyt studie med praktiserende i det nordøstlige Brasilien viser, at oplevelsen konsekvent udløste det, deltagerne beskrev som dyb omsorg og eksistentiel reorganisering—rigtige forandringer i deres liv og hvad der betyder noget for dem. Forskere gennemførte interviews med seks medlemmer af fællesskabet og integrerede sig i traditionen for at kortlægge disse erfaringer. Resultaterne bidrager med et vigtig stykke puslespil til voksende psykedelika-forskning: traditionelle kundskapssystemer er ikke bare interessante historiske artefakter, de er aktive tilgange til helbredelse og transformation som moderne videnskab stadig er ved at forstå.

items.title: Set, setting and substance in ayahuasca ceremonies and their association with altered self-awareness experiences: An exploratory investigation

summaries.en:
What you bring to an ayahuasca ceremony matters more than you might think. A new study of nearly 500 people found that your mindset going in—your psychological traits, spiritual beliefs, and how you tune into your own body—is the strongest predictor of whether you'll experience profound shifts in self-awareness like ego-dissolution. The dose intensity and what else you consume also play a role, but your inner landscape is the real game-changer.

Researchers surveyed participants before and after ceremonies, tracking their self-awareness experiences using established psychological measures. This fills an important gap: while we know psychedelics can help with depression and that ego-dissolution is linked to healing, we've known surprisingly little about what actually shapes these inner experiences. As psychedelic science matures beyond just measuring brain scans, understanding how set, setting, and substance work together is becoming crucial—it's the foundation for using these tools more thoughtfully and safely.
summaries.da:
Det, du bringer med dig til en ayahuasca-ceremoni, betyder mere end du måske tror. En ny undersøgelse af næsten 500 mennesker viser, at dit mindset før du starter—dine psykologiske træk, spirituelle overbevisninger og hvordan du er i kontakt med din egen krop—er den stærkeste forudsigelse for, om du oplever dybe skift i selvbevidsthed som ego-opløsning. Dosisintensiteten og hvad ellers du bruger spiller også en rolle, men dit indre landskab er det rigtige spil-skift.

Forskere spurgte deltagerne før og efter ceremonier og sporede deres selvbevidsthed ved hjælp af etablerede psykologiske mål. Dette udfylder et vigtig hul: selvom vi ved, at psykedelika kan hjælpe med depression og at ego-opløsning er forbundet med helbredelse, har vi vidst overraskende lidt om, hvad der faktisk former disse indre oplevelser.
